The secret weapon is creators, an underpriced asset in AEO. The post also discusses how to measure AEO beyond vanity metrics.

articles.title: UNGLAMOROUS
articles.summary: This post contains a list of 21 founders and the unglamorous work they did to bring their visions to life. The Pebble founders worked on their own factory line, Wakefit's founders acted as their own delivery men, and Stripe's founders did their IT support in person. The founders on this list spent time doing something that looked small: they shilled their own products, sent DMs nobody answered, and pretended to be their own users.

Stripe shows the SQL behind every answer, so a founder can check the math before it goes into an investor update. The Reports API stays free, and the Queries API is free until January 31.

articles.title: WHY WOULDN'T THE LABS DO IT?
articles.summary: Startups once feared Google entering their market, but today AI labs pose broader threats as their models cover most knowledge work. The labs' extensive capabilities can displace AI companies either through direct competition or by developing superior models. Successful tech ventures should aim to operate outside these labs' immediate focus areas, like in physical operations, proprietary data, or regulated workflows.

articles.title: SAAS S&M DOES NOT GET MORE EFFICIENT WITH SCALE
articles.summary: Most founders expect each sales and marketing dollar to buy more revenue once the company gets bigger. A VC firm checked 158 SaaS IPOs and found the median fell from $0.71 of new annual revenue per sales and marketing dollar the year before listing to $0.66 in the listing year. The 20 most recent IPOs had nearly twice the revenue at listing and still landed at $0.66, so the firm treats $0.50 to $0.70 as a normal range for a company that goes public. Some of the strongest companies listed well below it (Palantir came in at $0.33 and Snowflake at $0.57).
